\chapter{Learning Theory — Hoeffding}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.Hedge.Hoeffding
\section{Overview}

This module develops the analytic lemmas underlying Hoeffding's lemma for the Hedge
(multiplicative-weights) algorithm.  Starting from the convexity of the exponential
function, it derives a chain of bounds culminating in two log-MGF inequalities:
a weak bound with constant $\eta^2/2$ and a tight bound with constant $\eta^2/8$.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Product of a fraction and its complement]
\lean{mul_one_sub_le_quarter}
\label{mul_one_sub_le_quarter}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
For every real number $x$ with $0 \le x \le 1$, the product $x(1-x)$ is at most
$\tfrac{1}{4}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Convexity bound for the exponential]
\lean{exp_convexity_bound'}
\label{exp_convexity_bound'}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\eta$ be a real number and let $x \in [0,1]$. Then
\[
  e^{-\eta x} \;\le\; 1 - x + x\,e^{-\eta}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Weighted exponential sum versus affine upper bound]
\lean{weighted_exp_le_affine}
\label{weighted_exp_le_affine}
\leanok
\uses{exp_convexity_bound'}
\difficulty{3}
Let $p_1,\dots,p_n$ be a probability vector, that is $p_i \ge 0$ for every $i$ and
$\sum_{i} p_i = 1$, and let $\ell_1,\dots,\ell_n \in \bbr$ satisfy $0 \le \ell_i \le 1$
for every $i$. Then for every $\eta \in \bbr$,
\[
  \sum_{i} p_i\, e^{-\eta\,\ell_i}
  \;\le\;
  1 - \bigl(1 - e^{-\eta}\bigr)\sum_{i} p_i\,\ell_i.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The logarithmic inequality $\ln(1+u)\le u$]
\lean{log_one_add_le}
\label{log_one_add_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
For every real number $u > -1$, the natural logarithm satisfies $\ln(1+u) \le u$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A quadratic upper bound for $\eta - 1 + e^{-\eta}$]
\lean{eta_exp_bound}
\label{eta_exp_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
For every real number $\eta \ge 0$, the quantity $\eta - 1 + e^{-\eta}$ satisfies the
bound
\[
  \eta - 1 + e^{-\eta} \;\le\; \frac{\eta^2}{2}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Weak Hoeffding log-MGF bound]
\lean{hoeffding_log_mgf_weak}
\label{hoeffding_log_mgf_weak}
\leanok
\uses{eta_exp_bound}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n \ge 1$ and let $p = (p_1, \dots, p_n)$ be a probability vector, so that $p_i \ge
0$ for every $i$ and $\sum_{i} p_i = 1$. Let $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_n \in [0,1]$, and let
$\eta > 0$. Writing $L = \sum_{i} p_i \ell_i$ for the average loss, one has
\[
  \log\!\Bigl(\sum_{i} p_i\, e^{-\eta\, \ell_i}\Bigr)
  \;\le\;
  -\eta L + \frac{\eta^2}{2}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bernoulli MGF bound (Hoeffding's lemma)]
\lean{bernoulli_mgf_bound}
\label{bernoulli_mgf_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{7}
Let $L \in [0,1]$ and let $\eta$ be a real number. Then the moment generating function
of the shifted Bernoulli weight $1 - L + L\,e^{-\eta}$ satisfies
\[
  \ln\!\bigl(1 - L + L\,e^{-\eta}\bigr)
  \;\le\;
  -L\eta + \frac{\eta^2}{8}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Tight Hoeffding bound on the exponential loss]
\lean{hoeffding_log_mgf_tight}
\label{hoeffding_log_mgf_tight}
\leanok
\uses{bernoulli_mgf_bound, weighted_exp_le_affine}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p_1,\dots,p_n$ be a probability distribution, so $p_i \ge 0$ for every $i$ and
$\sum_{i=1}^n p_i = 1$, and let $\ell_1,\dots,\ell_n \in [0,1]$ be losses. Write $L =
\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\,\ell_i$ for the expected loss. Then for every $\eta > 0$,
\[
  \log\!\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\,e^{-\eta\,\ell_i}\Bigr)
  \;\le\;
  -\eta\,L + \frac{\eta^2}{8}.
\]
\end{theorem}
